user.title: Batocera
user.description: Connect a Batocera box. The MQTT integration must be set up first.

install.title: Install on the box
install.description: Home Assistant connects to the box over SSH as root, adds an SSH key of its own to root's authorized keys, and installs the ha-batocera daemon. From then on it uses that key to keep the daemon up to date.

data_description.name: The box's MQTT topics go under batocera/ and this name, in lower case, with underscores for spaces.
data_description.host: Host name or IP address of the box.
data_description.password: Batocera's default root password is linux. It is used for this install only and is not stored.
data_description.mqtt_host: The broker as the box reaches it: an address on your network, not core-mosquitto or localhost.
data_description.mqtt_user: An account for the box. Leave empty if the broker needs none.

manual.title: Box already set up
manual.description: Connect a box where the ha-batocera daemon was installed by hand.

data_description.topic: batocera/ and the device name set in ha-batocera.conf on the box.

reconfigure.title: Pair again
reconfigure.description: Home Assistant connects with the root password, trusts the SSH host key the box has now, replaces its own SSH key on the box and reinstalls the daemon. The settings on the box are kept.

data_description.password: Used for this step only, not stored.

error.invalid_topic: Enter a topic without wildcards (+ or #).
error.cannot_connect: Cannot connect to the box over SSH.
error.invalid_auth: The box refused the root password.
error.host_key_mismatch: The box's SSH host key changed during the install.
error.install_failed: The install failed on the box. The Home Assistant log has the details.

host_key_mismatch.title: {name}: SSH host key changed
host_key_mismatch.description:
The SSH host key of {name} ({host}) is not the one Home Assistant trusted when it was set up, so Home Assistant does not connect to it and does not update the ha-batocera daemon.

If Batocera was reinstalled or the key was replaced on purpose, reconfigure the Batocera integration for this box with the root password: it then trusts the new key. If not, something on your network may be posing as the box.

update_failed.title: {name}: cannot update ha-batocera
update_failed.description:
Home Assistant could not check or update the ha-batocera daemon on {name} ({host}): {error}

It tries again the next time the box comes online, or when the integration is reloaded. If the box no longer accepts Home Assistant's SSH key, reconfigure the Batocera integration for this box with the root password.

init.title: Who may play
init.description: Everyone who can open Home Assistant sees what is playing and browses the games. Launching, pausing and stopping games is for admins, and for the users picked here. Automations may always do it.

data.control_users: Users who may launch, pause and stop games
